Major (Rtd.) Md. Matiur Rahman and another ------Petitioners.
Vs.
The State ------ Opposite Party.
full_judgment:
Habibur Rahman Khan, J.: This application for bail under Section 498 Cr.P.C. having been moved on behalf of Major (Rtd) Md. Motiur Rahman and Md. Mofazzal Hossain accused in Pakundia, P.S. Case No. 6(12)/89 under Sections 364/342/346/323/379/34 of the Penal Code, a Rule was issued by this Court on 15.7.91 calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Kishoreganj, to show cause as to why the said accused petitioner shall not be released on bail in the aforesaid case. 

 2. The accused petitioners along with several others are accused in Pakundia P.S. Case No. 6(12)89 which was started consequent on the F.I.R. lodged by one Biswa Nath Kundu on 13.12.89. 

 3. In the case, out of 90 persons named in the F.I.R. 60 accused were arrested and out of them 58 have been released on bail by the Courts below. The accused petitioners were arrested on 13.12.89 at Kapasia within the District of Gazipur which is far away from the place of occurrence at Pakundia and since then they are in custody. 

 4. The occurrence is alleged to have taken place from 11.12.89 to 13.12.89 and the accused petitioners were arrested under Section 54 of the Criminal Procedure Code on 12.12.89 under Kapasia P.S.G.D. Entry No. 429 dt. 13.12.89 and thereafter were shown arrested in connection with the instant case on 20.12.89. The police after investigation submitted charge sheet on 18.1.91 under Sections 364/346/342/379 of the Penal Code. In the charge sheet it has been stated that 13 F.I.R. named accused died in the confrontation with the police. Besides this case being Pakundia, P.S. Case No. 6(12)89, consequent on the F.I.R. lodged by Biswa Nath Kundu, four other cases have been started against these two accused petitioners and those cases have arisen out of the same occurrence. In all the cases prayer for bail of these two accused petitioners was refused by the Court below. It is submitted that the accused petitioners are devoted Muslims engaged in imparting spiritual education to the people of the Country and they are innocent and allegations are totally baseless, fabricated, concocted, imaginary and have been made for covering up the attrocities of the police in the village committed by them on 11.12.89, 12.12.89 and 13.12.89 and the instant case has been made out for co-lateral purposes in order to harass and humiliate the accused petitioners before the public. The learned counsel submits that the allegations made in the F.I.R. do not constitute any offence for which the case has been started and the charge sheet has been submitted. Furthermore, there is no specific allegation against these accused petitioners so as to implicate with the commission of the offence. The learned counsel further submits that out of 60 accused persons arrested 58 have been enlarged on bail and these two accused petitioners who stand on the equal footing were not allowed to go on bail since the date of their arrest on 13.12.89 and the police took unusually long time to submit the charge sheet and even after completion of investigation and submission of charge sheet more than one year has elapsed and it is also not known as to when the trial will commence. On this ground alone, the learned Counsel submits that the prayer for bail of the accused petitioners deserves consideration. The learned Counsel for, the accused petitioners then submits that the learned Sessions Judge while rejecting the prayer for bail has not applied his judicial mind which is apparent from the order of the learned Sessions Judge passed on 30.3.90. It appears that the learned Sessions Judge has passed the order rejecting the prayer for bail as their prayer for bail was earlier on consideration and that there is a prima facie case against the petitioners. The prayer for bail having been rejected, they moved this Court for bail and obtained Rules in all the five cases'. Out of the five cases, in 3 cases F.I.R. has been lodged by the Officer-in-Charge of Pakundia Police Station and the case out of which the present Rule arises, the information was lodged by one Biswa Nath and the other case being Pakundia P.S. Case No. 5(12)89, F.I.R. was lodged by the constable Md. Joad Ali. Though informants are different persons, facts stated in the F.I.R. and the manner of occurrence disclosed in all the cases are almost the same. The police, after investigation, submitted charge sheet under different sections in different cases. As the allegation made in the charge sheet and the offences mentioned therein are different,' we will deal with the cases in 5 Misc. Cases separately, though there are certain common features in all the cases arising out of the same alleged occurrence. 

 5. Now let us take up Misc. Case No. 557 of 199.1 arising out of Pakundia P.s. Case No. 6(12)89 wherein application has been made by the two accused Persons for bail, their bail prayer having been rejected by the Sessions Judge. The F.I.R. of this case, as we have said, was filed by one Biswa Nath Kundu on 12.12.89 with the Pakundia Police Station. The Police, after investigation, submitted change sheet under Sections 364/346/342/379/344 of the Penal Code on 18.1.91. The accused petitioners were arrested on 13.12.89 from Kapasia Upazila and thereafter shown arrested in the instant case on 28.12.89. 

 6. In support of the prayer for bail made in the instant case, Mr. Moudud Ahmed, the learned Counsel appearing for the accused, submits that the learned Sessions Judge in rejecting the prayer for bail on 30.3.91 has not taken into consideration that the prayer for bail was rejected before the submission of the charge sheet and subsequent prayer was made at a time after the submission of the charge sheet while there remained little or no scope for tempering with the evidence by the accused petitioner. 

 7. Mr. A.F.M. Shahid, the learned Deputy Attorney General appearing for the State submits that the cases against the accused petitioners are of serious nature and the accused petitioner No. 1 is a very powerful man having so many followers and therefore he should not be released on bail as there is apprehension of tampering with the evidence. The learned Deputy Attorney General while explaining the delay in the matter of holding the trial submits that delay was caused not due to the laches of the prosecution but due to the fact that the other accused persons filed application for bail before the Sessions Judge for which the case could not be made ready for trial. It has been pointed out in the case of Manzoor and others Vs. The State, reported in P.L.D. 1972 (S.C.) 81(relevant page 84) that "Bail is not to be withheld as a punishment. There is no legal or moral compulsion to keep people in jail merely on the allegation that they have committed offences Punishable with death or transportation, unless reasonable grounds appear to exist to disclose their complicity. The ultimate conviction and incarceration of a guilty person can repair the wrong caused by a mistaken relief of interim bail granted to him, but no satisfactory reparation can be offered to an innocent man for his unjustified incarceration at any stage of the case, albeit his acquittal in the long run." 

 8. In the case of Ashraf Ali Mondal & ors. Vs. State and another reported in 1988 B.L.D. (A.D) 21, the prayer for bail was allowed when it was found that it was reasonable to grant bail and there is apprehension that the case may be further delayed and the appellant will suffer due to prolonged custody. 

 9. We have carefully perused the F.I.R., the Charge Sheet and the other materials placed before us. We do not find any material so as to distinguish the case of the accused petitioners with those of the others who have been released on bail. Since the Charge Sheet has been already submitted, we also do not find much force in the submission of the Deputy Attorney General that if the accused be released on bail, there will be scope for tampering with the evidence. Without entering into the merit of the case, which may prejudice either side, we like to Point out that the long delay in holding the trial and the apprehension expressed by the learned Counsel for the accused petitioner that the trial may be further delayed for one reason or the other seems to be reasonable as because the record has not yet been sent to the Sessions Judge for trial. In view of the above, we think it will be reasonable to allow the accused petitioners to be released on bail till the commencement the trial and we leave it for the trial Court to determine whether the accused petitioners should continue on bail during the trial also. 

 10. In the facts and circumstances, we are satisfied that it is a fit case in which the accused petitioners should be enlarged on bail till the trial commences. We, however, like to mention that whatever observations we may have made in disposing of the application, is for the limited purpose of bail and we are not to be understood to have decided any matter touching the merit of the case.
